response.rationale: Both forms ordinarily mean a plastic bag used to carry purchases. Indonesian commonly uses “kantong plastik,” while Malaysian commonly uses “beg plastik,” making this a useful everyday lexical contrast.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Kantong plastik” may be understood in Malaysia, but “beg plastik” is the ordinary Malaysian preference; the reverse pairing is likewise not the ordinary Indonesian preference.
